newsitem.title: GERMANY: Selective buys send German DAX to new record.
newsitem.headline: Selective buys send German DAX to new record.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip DAX index hit a new record high on Wednesday following the Federal Reserve's decision to leave U.S. rates unchanged, against widespread expectations for a moderate rate hike.
The 30-share DAX hit an alltime high of 2,651.49 in early dealings, just above its old record of 2,650.49, before slipping to trade at 2,649.96, up 11.51 points.

Dealers said initial worries at the dollar's slide after the U.S. rate decision -- which sent shares briefly lower in pre-bourse trade -- had given way to selective buying, with the chemical sector still in the limelight.
"People are looking for the solid stocks," said one dealer.
Although some noted that German equities are looking dangerously overbought at current levels, most dealers said the market's bull run still had some more power behind it.
Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell on Tuesday evening issued a report saying German equities remained an attractive buy.
"I could see this taking us (the DAX) to 2,670," said a Frankfurt trader, but added that this was an unlikely target for Wednesday, with trading still hesitant overall.
"Uncertainty is not out of this market yet," he said.
Giant chemical groups BASF AG and Bayer AG dominated early trade again, with gains of 87 pfennigs to 48.93 and 25 pfennigs to 56.63 marks respectively, both on healthy volumes.
